name: mnemic_spatial_erosion_architect_ai
label: The Architect of Erosion
godotFeature: NavigationServer3D & PhysicsServer3D for dynamic environment modification
poeticVision: The chilling dread of the memory-world itself betraying you. Imagine running across a crumbling path, only for an unseen force to actively erase the ground behind you, making retreat impossible. The next platform you eye flickers out of existence, or reconfigures into a maze of unstable fragments. This entity doesn't just chase; it intelligently rewrites the very reality Lyra is trying to traverse, making every step a gamble against the total dissolution of space. It's the silent horror of the world forgetting itself, making you doubt not just your path, but the certainty of existence itself.
usage: Attach this script to a Node3D in your scene (e.g., named 'Architect'). Set the 'lyra_node_path' export variable to the NodePath of Lyra's CharacterBody3D node. Ensure your memory fragments are individual Node3D scenes, each containing a child StaticBody3D (named 'StaticBody3D'), a NavigationRegion3D (named 'NavigationRegion3D'), and optionally a MeshInstance3D (named 'MeshInstance3D'). Add all these root MemoryFragment Node3D nodes to the 'ErodibleFragment' group. The Architect will then dynamically erode or reconfigure these fragments within 'erosion_range' of Lyra, affecting their collision and navigation.

parameters.name: lyra_node_path
parameters.description: The NodePath to Lyra's CharacterBody3D node in the scene.

parameters.name: erosion_range
parameters.description: The maximum distance from Lyra within which memory fragments are considered for erosion or reconfiguration.

parameters.name: erosion_interval
parameters.description: The time in seconds between each erosion/reconfiguration cycle performed by the Architect.

parameters.name: reconfiguration_chance
parameters.description: The probability (0.0 to 1.0) that a selected memory fragment will be reconfigured (moved/rotated/shape-swapped) instead of being fully eroded.

dependencies: StaticBody3D (as a child of each memory fragment, named 'StaticBody3D')
CollisionShape3D (as children of StaticBody3D, for fragment collision)
MeshInstance3D (optional, as a child of each memory fragment, named 'MeshInstance3D', for visual representation)
NavigationRegion3D (as a child of each memory fragment, named 'NavigationRegion3D', for navigation mesh updates)
All manipulable memory fragment Node3D nodes must be added to the 'ErodibleFragment' group.
verdict: The Architect of Erosion masterfully transmutes the very fabric of memory into a relentless, intelligent hunter, ensuring Lyra's desperate race is a constant, terrifying dance with oblivion.
impact: The Architect of Erosion will fundamentally transform the player's relationship with the game world, turning the environment from a passive backdrop into an active, intelligent, and deeply unsettling antagonist. Players will experience constant paranoia and urgency as the very ground beneath them is actively erased or reconfigured, forcing split-second decisions and fostering a profound sense of existential dread. This mechanic ensures that every step is a gamble, every path a potential trap, and every moment a desperate struggle against the world's own dissolution, perfectly mirroring Lyra's internal battle against forgetting.
